item.title: Hyperrigidity and convexity in two variables
item.description: arXiv:2611.03716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend Brown's one-variable rigidity theorem to strictly convex functions of two variables under a regularity assumption. Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let $f$ be real-valued, strictly convex on $K$, and of class $C^2$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. We prove that the generating set $\{x_1,x_2,f\}$ is hyperrigid in $C(K)$.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Pietrzycki

item.title: Small Hankel operators on weighted Besov spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.03901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize bounded small Hankel operators from $B_p(\om)$ to $\overline{B_q(\om)}$ on the polydisc for $0<p,q<\infty$, under explicit conditions relating the kernel parameter to the weight. When $q<p$, boundedness is equivalent to a weighted Besov condition on the symbol; when $p\le q$, it is equivalent to a weighted supremum condition on a shifted radial derivative. In particular, the diagonal case is characterized by the product Bloch space. The proof combines weighted Bergman duality and atomic factorization with local kernel estimates and randomized atomic tests.
item.dc:creator: Chen Li, Kai Wang

item.title: A Hardy space approximation supporting zero-free half-planes for the $\zeta$-function
item.description: arXiv:2611.03924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By a theorem of Bagchi, the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds if and only if $E(s) = 1/s$ belongs to the closed linear span of $G_k(s) = (k^{-s} - k^{-1})\zeta(s)/s$, $k \geq 2$, in the Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb{C}_{1/2})$, where $\mathbb{C}_\alpha$ is the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s) > \alpha$. The formal M\"obius expansion $E = \sum_{k \geq 2} \mu(k) G_k$ diverges on the critical line, by a theorem of B\'aez-Duarte. We study it in the scale of spaces $H^2(\mathbb{C}_\alpha)$, where its convergence forces $\zeta$ to be zero-free in $\mathbb{C}_\alpha$. We prove that the partial sums $S_n$ converge to $E$ in $H^2(\mathbb{C}_\alpha)$ for every $\alpha > 1$, and that a single zero of $\zeta$ in $\mathbb{C}_\alpha$ keeps the best-approximation error $d_n(\alpha)^2$ uniformly away from zero. We express the M\"obius error $s_n(\alpha) = \|S_n - E\|^2_\alpha$ as a series with elementary terms, free of $\zeta$, and compute it for $n \leq 10^6$: $s_n(1/2)$ oscillates without decaying, whereas for $\alpha > 1/2$ it decays at a rate close to $n^{1-2\alpha}$, much faster than the bound known under RH. On the critical line, $d_n(1/2)^2$ behaves like $0.046/\log n$ for $100 \leq n \leq 5120$, in agreement with earlier computations by B\'aez-Duarte, Balazard, Landreau and Saias.
item.dc:creator: Juan Manzur, Gustavo Quintero

item.title: Pseudo-Fredholm operators form a regularity on Hilbert spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.04004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space. We prove that the class of pseudo-Fredholm operators on $H$ is a regularity in the sense of Kordula and M\"uller. We also prove that the classes of left and right generalized Drazin invertible operators are regularities on $H$. Consequently, the generalized Kato spectrum and the corresponding generalized Drazin spectra satisfy the spectral mapping theorem. We construct an operator $T$ on a separable complex Banach space such that $T^2$ is right generalized Drazin invertible whereas $T$ is not pseudo-Fredholm. In particular, the power axiom need not hold for pseudo-Fredholm operators on Banach spaces. Finally, we show that the accumulation sets of the approximate point and surjectivity spectra define regularities on Banach spaces, yielding another proof of the regularity of generalized Drazin invertible operators in $\B(X)$.
item.dc:creator: Zakariae Aznay, Fadil Chabbabi, Hassan Zariouh

item.title: Revisiting the Upper Bild of Quaternionic Numerical Ranges
item.description: arXiv:2611.04044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The upper bild of the quaternionic numerical range provides a convex representative of the generally nonconvex quaternionic numerical range. Although its convexity is known, the geometry of the upper bild is difficult to describe explicitly, even for 2-by-2 quaternionic matrices. In this paper, we revisit the upper bild of quaternionic numerical ranges from both algebraic and geometric viewpoints. We first point out gaps in Kumar's proof. We then investigate several special classes of 2-by-2 quaternionic matrices and describe their shapes and boundary structures in the closed upper complex half-plane directly in terms of the standard eigenvalues and the off-diagonal entry of the Schur form. For the general 2-by-2 case, we use a different canonical form. Following So and Thompson, we prove the concavity of the upper-boundary function through the associated complex representation. For the lower boundary, we obtain a distance-to-a-disk representation and use convex optimization to prove its convexity. We also treat the degenerate cases. Together with the connectedness of the vertical sections, these results give an alternative proof of the convexity of the upper bild for arbitrary quaternionic matrices.
item.dc:creator: Jie Tian, Tin-Yau Tam

item.title: Tensor preduals, positive homogeneity and harmonicity in two-Lipschitz spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.04562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study subspaces of two-Lipschitz mappings using group actions and tensor preduals. We first show that the ambient spaces contain large classical sequence spaces. We then use similarity actions to select smaller subspaces. Character-equivariant mappings form weak$^*$-closed fixed-point spaces and admit quotient tensor preduals. We give two applications. For mappings on Banach spaces, we describe positive homogeneity in each variable and construct bounded projections. For mappings on finitely generated groups, we characterize harmonicity in each variable. We show that the harmonic predual is the projective tensor product of the corresponding one-variable quotient preduals.
item.dc:creator: Arindam Mandal

item.title: Weighted orbits of hypercyclic vectors on F-spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.04629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study $\mathcal{F}$-hypercyclicity of weighted orbits $\lambda_nT^nx$ for continuous linear operators $T$ on complex F-spaces, where $\mathcal{F}$ is a Furstenberg family with the cut--shift--and--paste (CuSP) property. We characterize the scalar sequences for which weighted hypercyclicity always implies ordinary hypercyclicity: their nonzero values must be bounded and bounded away from zero. The same condition removes weights for every such family. For the converse inclusion, we prove that a bounded scalar sequence preserves all $\mathcal{F}$-hypercyclic vectors if its backward-shift $\omega$-limit system is distal and does not contain the zero sequence. For chaotic operators, minimality of this system suffices. In particular, every complex nilsequence which is not identically zero preserves $\mathcal{F}$-hypercyclicity, and equality holds when its nonzero values are bounded away from zero. We also obtain simultaneous weighted return results and stability under unimodular weights with asymptotically trivial multiplicative differences.
item.dc:creator: Jian Li, Yonghang Ruan, Yini Yang

item.title: Characterization of Integral Transforms for Hilbert Space-Valued Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.04698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of this paper is to characterize the Fourier transform of functions taking values in a separable Hilbert space $\Hi$ and defined on locally compact abelian groups. Inspired by Krukowskis characterization of integral transforms on locally compact abelian groups, we establish characterizations of the Fourier, Laplace, and cosine transforms for separable Hilbert space-valued functions on locally compact abelian groups. Furthermore, we obtain a characterization of the group Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group.
item.dc:creator: Satyajyoti Achar, Ramesh Manna

item.title: Real-analytic functional calculus and strictly real Banach algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.04758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use real-analytic functional calculus to show that the envelope of the algebra of $m$-variable polynomials with real coefficients, with respect to the class of strictly real Banach algebras, is isomorphic to the algebra of real-valued analytic functions on $\mathbb{R}^m$.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Aristov

item.title: Matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces and tent spaces:characterizations, duality and interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2611.04810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, $0<p<\infty$, $0<q,r\le\infty$, and $W$ be a matrix $\mathcal A_p$ weight on ${\mathbb R}^n$. We introduce the matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces $Z^{p,q,r}_\alpha(W)$ and tent spaces $T^{p,q,r}_\alpha(W)$ on the upper half-space and establish their characterizations using reducing operators. We then characterize homogeneous matrix-weighted Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces in terms of the corresponding $Z$-spaces and tent spaces, respectively, using Schwartz kernels satisfying Tauberian and finite moment conditions. Furthermore, we establish duality for the matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces and tent spaces and obtain real and complex interpolation results for these spaces and the associated homogeneous matrix-weighted Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces.
item.dc:creator: Tengfei Bai, Pengfei Guo, Jingshi Xu

item.title: Dissipative Hamiltonian representations of linear evolution equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.05063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate explicit and implicit dissipative Hamiltonian representations of generators of strongly continuous semigroups on real or complex Hilbert spaces. For a prescribed positive definite selfadjoint energy operator $H$ satisfying $\operatorname{dom}(A)\subset\operatorname{dom}(H)$, we show that the Lyapunov dissipation inequality is equivalent to an exact factorization $A=DH$, where $D$ can be chosen maximally dissipative. For bounded $H$, the criterion also yields an implicit representation. We further study energy constructions based on closed intertwiners and output trajectories, distinguishing contractive energy-space dynamics from operator factorizations on the original state space. Examples illustrate the roles of noncoercivity, unboundedness, and domain compatibility.
item.dc:creator: Volker Mehrmann, Timo Reis

item.title: On the Gabor frame set of polynomial-Gaussian windows
item.description: arXiv:2611.05337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove two sufficient conditions for the frame property of Gabor systems $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)=\{e^{2\pi i mb\,\cdot}g(\cdot-ak):k,m\in\mathbb{Z} \}$ generated by polynomial--Gaussian windows $g(t)=P(t)e^{-ct^2}$, where $c>0$ and $P$ is a nonzero complex polynomial of degree $n$. The conditions depend only on the product $ab$ of the lattice parameters and the degree of $P$. First, $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$ is a frame whenever $ab<1$ is irrational. Second, if $ab=p/q<1$, with $p,q\in\mathbb{N}$ coprime, then $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$ is a frame whenever $q-p>n$. Consequently, in the region $ab<1$, failure of the frame property can occur only on rational hyperbolas whose reduced denominator and numerator differ by at most $n$. The proof extends the translated-Wronskian method of Faulhuber and Petersen [\emph{The frame set of the first Hermite function}, arXiv:2609.02610] from the first Hermite function to arbitrary polynomial multiples of a Gaussian, combining a multiplicity estimate for Wronskians with Jensen's formula.
item.dc:creator: Jakob Lemvig

item.title: Weak uniqueness and autonomous approximation for the SLE-reversible Weil-Petersson response diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2611.04417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the self-consistent common-noise equation associated with the Weil--Petersson response differential of the rotationally marked SLE welding probability. For $0<\kappa\leq4$, we prove joint weak uniqueness among continuous adapted weak solutions whose law at each deterministic time is the welding probability, and obtain the Markov property in the original filtration. A conditional Gaussian lift and capacity localization give the required $L^1$ generator-range density. Identification with the canonical law gives stationarity and reversibility. We also construct autonomous Fej\'er and Poisson regularizations with pathwise-unique global strong solutions. Their joint state-noise laws converge to the canonical law for every initial probability absolutely continuous with respect to the welding probability.
item.dc:creator: Chunhao Cai

item.title: Space-Time HWI Inequalities and the Wasserstein Current for Kinetic Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.04831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a space-time analogue of the HWI inequality of Otto-Villani for controlled kinetic equations with a semiconvex confining potential. It bounds the time-averaged relative entropy by spatial and conditional velocity transport distances, the velocity Fisher information, an intrinsic action of the path, and a boundary term given by the time endpoint values of the Wasserstein current. The key step is a differential comparison inequality for the Wasserstein current, which captures the transfer of dissipation from velocity to position. Along the Langevin semigroup, this inequality yields a kinetic evolution variational inequality involving the second time derivative of the squared spatial Wasserstein distance and a damping term. Under a compatible spatial Talagrand's transport inequality, we obtain a boundary-free space-time logarithmic Sobolev inequality on every interval $[0,T]$, $T>0$, with the optimal $T^{-2}$ short-time scaling of the constant. As a consequence, we also establish entropy decay for every friction coefficient and every initial density of finite entropy, with optimal cubic order at short times and exponential decay at long times.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Li, Jianfeng Lu

item.title: Hereditarily Lindel\"of and hereditarily separable subspaces of function spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.04911v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A space is ESLC if it contains neither an $S$-space nor an $L$-space, and NFS is the class of spaces containing no free sequences of length $\omega_1$. We prove that under $\mathrm{MA}(\omega_1)$, if all finite powers of $X$ belong to NFS, then $C_p(X)^\omega$ is ESLC; thus, for subspaces of $C_p(X)$, hereditary Lindel\"ofness, hereditary separability and countable spread coincide. This is derived from a dual form of a theorem of Todor\v{c}evi\'c. A Lindel\"of $\Sigma$-space belongs to NFS if and only if its compact subspaces have countable tightness. Hence $C_p(X)$ contains no $L$-spaces if $X$ is a Lindel\"of $\Sigma$-space of countable tightness and $\mathrm{MA}(\omega_1)$ holds, or if $X$ is any Lindel\"of $\Sigma$-space and PFA holds. Under $\mathrm{MA}(\omega_1)$, all iterated function spaces of Corson compact spaces are ESLC, and in ZFC the space $C_p(X,\{0,1\})$ is ESLC for every zero-dimensional Corson compact space $X$.
item.dc:creator: Evgenii Reznichenko

item.title: O-segments on topological measure spaces
item.description: arXiv:0806.1247v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mu$ be a finite non-atomic measure on a set $X$. A \emph{segment} for $\mu$ is an increasing family $u(t)$, $t\in[0,1]$, of measurable sets with $u(0)=\emptyset$, $u(1)=X$ and $\mu(u(t))=t\,\mu(X)$; by a theorem of Fryszkowski, finitely many measures $f\,d\mu$ admit a common segment. We study \emph{open segments}, i.e.\ segments consisting of open sets, when $X$ carries a topology. We show that weak outer regularity of $\mu$ is equivalent to the approximability of measurable sets by open sets, and that it holds for every finite Borel measure on a metrizable space. Our main result states that if $\mu$ is finite, non-atomic and weakly outer regular, then for all $f,g\in L^1(\mu)$ with $(\int f\,d\mu,\int g\,d\mu)\neq(0,0)$ there is a common open segment for $f\,d\mu$ and $g\,d\mu$; in particular, for every $f\in L^1(\mu)$ there is an open segment for $\mu$ which is simultaneously a segment for $f\,d\mu$. Relative versions allow one to prescribe an initial set. We also characterize open segments as upper semicontinuous functions with uniform distribution and show that on separable metrizable spaces a single measure admits such a function which is continuous.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: A Note On Majorizing Norms on Majorized Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2111.06758v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a new type of norm for ordered vector spaces majorized by a proper (convex) cone that generalizes the notions of order unit norm and base norm. Then we give sufficient conditions to ensure its completeness. In the case of normed Riesz spaces, we also present necessary completeness conditions and describe the completed norm. Finally, we define a particular family of well-behaving sets. Spaces majorized by the cone generated by these sets display surprisingly interesting structural properties. In particular, we generalize two famous standard results in Banach lattice theory. Namely, every principal ideal in a Banach lattice is an AM-space and every Banach lattice having a generating cone with a compact base admits an equivalent L-norm.
item.dc:creator: Vasco Schiavo

item.title: The Ces\`aro Operator, Rhaly operators, and the Toeplitz Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2608.25740v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Barr\'{\i}a and Halmos [\emph{Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.} (1982), (10) Example] asked whether the Ces\`aro operator belongs to the Toeplitz algebra. We answer this question affirmatively and prove that the Ces\`aro operator is the product of a Toeplitz operator and a continuous function of a self-adjoint Toeplitz operator. Rhaly operators are a natural generalization of the Ces\`aro operator. We give necessary and sufficient conditions for a Rhaly operator to belong to the Toeplitz algebra or the Hankel algebra. The main approach is to use the Fej\'er kernels to get localized estimates for operators. This yields a necessary condition for an operator to belong to the Hankel algebra. As an application, we find a class of Rhaly operators that are asymptotic Toeplitz operators and essentially commute with the unilateral shift, but are not in the Hankel algebra. This answers (17) Question in the same paper.
item.dc:creator: Yuanqi Sang

item.title: Noncommutative sharp Hausdorff-Young inequality
item.description: arXiv:2609.10424v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the sharp Hausdorff--Young inequality on quantum euclidean spaces. Our result implies the sharp Hausdorff--Young constants for the Weyl transform. The key ingredients are a sharp Hessian comparison inequality and a novel flow related to the mixed- norm of noncommutative Gabor transform; the Hessian comparison leads to the monotonicity of the flow. We also apply the same flow technique to prove the sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities on Heisenberg groups and the affine group.
item.dc:creator: Hongsen Qiu, Xiao Xiong

item.title: Sharp Riesz capacity inequalities and the P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.04811v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $n\geq2$ and $p\in(n-2,n)$, we prove that closed balls maximize the ratio of Riesz $p$-capacity to Newtonian capacity among all compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$. This resolves the classical P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} capacity ratio conjecture and its higher-dimensional extensions. For $n\geq4$, a sharp inequality for the ratio of Newtonian capacity to logarithmic capacity is established. All equality cases are characterized.
item.dc:creator: Mengwei Su, Qiang Sun, Ge Xiong

item.title: Zero products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Bergman space of the unit ball
item.description: arXiv:2610.26139v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, using local boundary factorizations of harmonic functions and singular-value estimates for Toeplitz products, we study the zero-product problem for Toeplitz operators on the Bergman space of the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We prove that a finite product of such operators is zero only if one of the symbols is identically zero, provided that all the symbols are harmonic on the open unit ball and continuous on the closed unit ball.
item.dc:creator: Jiawei Wang, Xianfeng Zhao

item.title: Selection spectra and sharp perturbations of normal sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.38853v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a bounded sequence $y=(y_n)\subset E^*$ and $p>0$, put $G_p(y)=\{x\in E:(y_n(x))\in\ell_p\}$ and call $y$ $p$-strongly normal when $G_p(y)$ is dense in $E$. We study the density spectra of the original sequence, its subsequences, and its normalized successive blocks. The possible subsequence and block spectra are exactly $\varnothing$, $(0,\infty)$, $(1,\infty)$, $[r,\infty)$, and $(r,\infty)$ for $r>1$, and their possible pairs are precisely the nested pairs. Every such pair has a normalized weakly null $1$-unconditional basic realization in $\ell_1(\mathfrak c)^*$, even with empty original-sequence spectrum. Without a basicness requirement, the possible original-sequence spectra are all upper subsets of $(0,\infty)$; each is realized in a separable Hilbert space. We determine the exact universal perturbation classes: $\ell_p$ for a fixed original-sequence exponent, $c_0$ for the subsequence spectrum, and $\ell_1$ for the block spectrum. The ideal-valued version holds for every proper solid permutation-invariant linear ideal $c_{00}\subset A\subsetneq c_0$, without a norm or completeness assumption. For the author's 2012 selection model, the bounded-run criterion extends to all proper symmetric quasi-Banach sequence ideals. In the unbounded-run case, a single norm-one projection annihilates the summability domains of any family of fewer than $\mathfrak b$ such ideals; the quotient by their closed linear span contains a $1$-complemented isometric copy of $\ell_\infty$. Such copies also occur in the left jump at every $q>1$ and in the right jump at every $q\ge1$ of the scale of closed summability domains. Thus the common density criterion coexists with two-sided complemented discontinuities.
item.dc:creator: Wies{\l}aw \'Sliwa

item.title: Perturbations of Truncated Toeplitz operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.40295v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the structure of kernels of finite-rank perturbations of truncated Toeplitz operators. By realizing a perturbed truncated Toeplitz operator on a model space as a suitable matrix-valued truncated Toeplitz operator on an enlarged model space, we identify its kernel with a coordinate projection of the kernel of an associated block Toeplitz operator. This realization enables us to transfer the nearly $S^*$-invariant structure of Toeplitz kernels to the perturbed truncated setting. More precisely, for a perturbation of rank at most $n$, we show that the kernel of the perturbed truncated Toeplitz operator is nearly $S^*$-invariant with defect at most $2n+1$. We then extend the method to truncated Toeplitz operators on multiband spaces. In this setting, a perturbation of rank at most $n$ again preserves the finite-defect nearly $S^*$-invariant structure of the kernel, with the explicit upper bound $2n+2$ for the defect.
item.dc:creator: Arup Chattopadhyay, Arshad Khan

item.title: Sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities for solvable and semisimple Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.02597v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we obtain the sharp constants for Hausdorff--Young inequalities on simply connected, completely solvable Lie groups, and connected real semisimple Lie groups with finite center.
item.dc:creator: Jinsong Wu, Fulin Yang

item.title: Frame Properties of Effective Stationary Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2611.03358v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Kaczmarz algorithm is an iterative projection method for reconstructing vectors in a Hilbert space from inner product data. However, sequences that are effective for this algorithm need not be frames and may lack standard frame reconstruction properties. We investigate these properties for stationary effective sequences, which were classified by Kwapie\'n and Mycielski according to their spectral measures. In particular, we show that the corresponding Kaczmarz reconstruction series always converge unconditionally if and only if the spectral measure is atomic with finitely many point masses. We show that if the spectral measure is atomic, the stationary effective sequence and its auxiliary Parseval frame can be interchanged in the Kaczmarz reconstruction formula. Finally, we construct two stationary effective sequences with singular continuous spectral measures, one of which can be interchanged with its auxiliary Parseval frame in the reconstruction formula, and one of which cannot be interchanged.
item.dc:creator: Chad Berner, John E. Herr, Palle E. T. Jorgensen

item.title: Kadison--Singer in Deterministic Polynomial Time
item.description: arXiv:2609.17266v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given rational Hermitian matrices $H_1,\dots,H_N$ of rank at most one, finds signs $s\in\{\pm1\}^N$ with $\|\sum_i s_i H_i\|\le 13\|\sum_i H_i^2\|^{1/2}$. As a corollary, for vectors $v_i$ with $\sum_i v_iv_i^*=I$ and $\|v_i\|^2\le\delta$, the signs yield a partition $[N] = S_1 \cup S_2$ such that each part satisfies $\|\sum_{i \in S_j} v_i v_i^* - \frac{I}{2}\| \leq \frac{13}{2}\sqrt\delta$ for $j = 1,2$. This gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the Kadison--Singer problem, in Weaver's equivalent discrepancy-theoretic $\mathsf{KS}_2$ formulation, with a universal constant.
item.dc:creator: Ekene Ezeunala, Haotian Jiang

item.title: The e-Property for Quantum Markov Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.00703v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(\mathcal{T}_t)_{t\geqslant0}$ be a quantum Markov semigroup on a von Neumann algebra and let $\mathcal{A}$ be an invariant Feller $C^*$-algebra. We formulate the $e$-property on the full state space and show that its quantitative defect is equivalent, within an optimal factor two, to the Hausdorff measure of non-compactness of observable orbits. We develop Ces\`aro and Lip-norm criteria and a generalised Doeblin minorisation by a state-space contracting positive map, including finite-dimensional and measure-prepare factorisations. When every observable has the $e$-property, the Jacobs--de Leeuw--Glicksberg decomposition identifies the reversible Choi--Effros algebra and the norm-stable sector. Expected and decoherence-free subalgebras transfer the property under norm decay of the complementary dynamics, including infinite-dimensional ultracontractive and finite-index Pimsner--Popa regimes. Finally, we establish the full comparison hierarchy among ordinary, eventual, Ces\`aro and pointwise eventual equicontinuity notions, reinforced by matrix Jamison and homoclinic flow counterexamples. Projection-face criteria are treated in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Kania, Mariusz Niwi\'nski

item.title: Spectral Theory and Continuum Norm Resolvent Convergence of a One-Sided Discrete Dirac-Type Operator
item.description: arXiv:2611.00820v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate a one-dimensional discrete Dirac-type operator $D_d$ acting on the Hilbert space $\big(\ell^2(\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$, obtained from the classical continuous free Dirac operator by replacing the spatial derivative with the one-sided backward difference operator $I - S_1$, where $S_1$ denotes the right shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})$. We establish the fundamental operator-theoretic and spectral properties of $D_d$: unlike symmetric or supersymmetric lattice discretizations, $D_d$ is bounded and non-normal for every non-zero rest mass $m > 0$, with self-commutator $[D_d, D_d^\dag] = -2mc^3(-\Delta_{\mathrm{disc}})\sigma_2$, yet it is quadratically normal. We compute the exact operator norm, determine the exact spectral radius in two mass regimes, and show via Fourier--Laurent analysis that the spectrum $\sigma(D_d)$ is purely continuous and lies on a two-component algebraic curve in the complex plane undergoing a topological transition at $mc^2 = 2c$. Finally, introducing a lattice spacing $h > 0$ and embedding $\big(\ell^2(h\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$ isometrically into $\big(L^2(\mathbb{R};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$ via Whittaker--Shannon band-limited interpolation, we prove that the scaled non-normal discrete Dirac-type operator $D_{d,h}$ converges to the continuous self-adjoint Dirac operator $D$ in the norm resolvent sense at the optimal rate $\mathcal{O}(h)$ as $h \to 0^+$, without requiring frequency cutoffs.
item.dc:creator: Mariusz Niwi\'nski
